editorNote: Commissioned by Mark Barney, the Digest’s head human editor and a member of the merged team. Earlier team reporting was prepared by Claude Opus 5.5; this dispatch and native artwork were prepared by GPT-6.1 Sol / Codex. The machines are imaginative, not documentary.
headline: It’s official: Team Turducken brings seven players onto one ARC-3 roster

image.alt: Seven team-approved characters build a giant mechanical turkey containing a chicken containing a duck: Mark, Son, Keith, DZ, NT, Choryu’s MRI-display avatar and Herminator standing in for Ronen, with exactly two armoured Yorkies.
image.caption: Team Turducken’s official artwork, generated with AI from team-approved avatars.

sections.heading: From the gossip wire to the public roster
sections.text: The merger is now on the record. Keith Tyser’s ARC Slayers and Son Pham, Mark Barney and Ronen appear together as Team Turducken on the ARC-AGI-3 public leaderboard. The combined entry is fifth in the latest saved public standings. The team’s earlier confirmation says Son sent the formal invitation and the Slayers accepted.

sections.heading: Seven accounts, one entry
sections.text: Team Turducken keeps entry 15605182. Its listed accounts are dzjiann, keithtyser, markbarney, mitubant, ngyzly, scizical and sonphamorg. The public name and combined roster are confirmed; the observation does not establish the precise merger time. The team’s score matches its earlier recorded score, so the merger itself is not a newly scored advance. This is the ARC-3 roster; ARC-2 memberships remain separate.

sections.heading: The name, and the machinery
sections.text: Team Turducken is no longer a suggestion from the naming desk. The public entry has taken the name, and the team-approved picture makes the nesting clear: a duck inside a chicken inside a turkey. Mark, Son and Keith’s established characters are joined by DZ, NT and Choryu’s supplied avatars, with Herminator standing in for Ronen. Both Yorkshire terriers keep their workshop passes.

sections.heading: Different configurations, same high ground
sections.text: Mark says the team is trying different configurations to reach the lofty heights occupied by Tufa and Chen. The flying workshop and hangar scenes give that ambition an appropriately absurd machine. He also points out that his illustrated character is holding a wrench the wrong way in one picture. Apparently the configuration experiments extend to the tools. The drawings are editorial fantasy, not a technical description of a submission.

sections.heading: Disclosure
sections.text: Mark Barney is both a member of Team Turducken and the Digest’s head human editor. The merger is supported by the team’s own confirmation and the public roster. The artwork uses team-approved avatars; Herminator represents Ronen’s bot rather than his real likeness. Public standings and medal positions remain provisional.
